text:
alex: Hey infra team — I'm opening this thread because I'm blocked on cloud account setup for a new GPU cluster in eu-west-1. Need quota increases for ~16 A100 GPUs and more IPs for the node pools. Trying to avoid running into per-node pod/IP limits. Anyone done the quota flow for this account recently?

maria: Which instance family exactly? A100s are typically p4 or p4d — the AWS quota lines are different for each. Also need to know if you'll use EKS managed nodegroups or self-managed (kops/eksctl) so we can advise CNI config.

alex: We'll run EKS with mixed nodepools: heavy workers on p4d.xlarge (4x A100?) — actually planning p4d.24xlarge for throughput but also smaller g4dn/g5 for cheaper workloads. Goal: 16 GPUs live at steady state, burst to 24.

chen: OK. Two separate problems: 1) EC2 GPU quota (On-Demand/Spot limits per instance type) and 2) ENI / IP limits per instance type -> impacts max pods per node. For p4d.24xlarge the ENI/pod limits are pretty high but not infinite. EKS sets a default max pods per node based on that.

maria: Action items: 1) Open AWS support case requesting increases for the specific instance "Running On-Demand P4d instances" and the VPC elastic IP / ENI limits if you plan to attach many secondary IPs. 2) Request a higher "EC2 Instances" quota in eu-west-1 for the SKUs you plan to use (list all SKUs). 3) If using EKS, request quota bump for EBS/ENI/NetworkInterface quotas in that region.

alex: Any suggested wording for the support case? Trying to avoid back-and-forth.

maria: Copy/paste this into the AWS case: 

```
We're provisioning a production EKS cluster for model inference in eu-west-1. We require increases for the following quotas to support a dedicated GPU nodepool:
- Running On-Demand P4d (p4d.24xlarge): +8 (target total 12)
- Running On-Demand G5/G4dn (g5.12xlarge/g4dn.12xlarge): +10
- EC2 Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI): +200
- VPC IPv4 address quota (secondary IPs): +2048
Please validate network resource availability in eu-west-1 and advise on any regional constraints. We plan to use EKS with VPC CNI (aws-node) and ENI Trunking / Prefix Delegation.
```

chen: Also include that you'll be using ENI Trunking / Prefix Delegation and may need per-instance ENI configs (eniConfig) for nodegroups. That speeds up approval.

alex: Thanks. Quick question about pod density: what's the practical limit we should target per GPU node? Default EKS/kubelet max pods is driven by CNI and instance type but we might want to set a custom --max-pods to avoid hitting the ENI limit.

dana: Right — for GPUs we often run 1–4 pods per GPU depending on model memory. If you want high pod density (many small replicas) you run into IP exhaustion. Options:
- Use larger instance types and fewer pods per node (lower IP consumption)
- Enable VPC CNI prefix delegation so each ENI can host many more IPs
- Use a secondary network overlay (e.g., Calico with IP-in-IP) so pods use overlay IPs instead of ENI IPs (tradeoff: performance + NAT/masking)
- Use NVIDIA MIG on A100 to carve multiple GPU instances and schedule more workloads per host while keeping pod count moderate

maria: Also consider using multiple nodegroups: one nodegroup with large p4d nodes (low pod density, high GPU count), and another with g5/g4 for lightweight inference. Karpenter or Cluster Autoscaler can help with heterogeneous scaling.

alex: Can you paste the commands to check current EKS/Ec2 quotas and per-node pod allocatable?

chen: Sure: 

```
# Check nodes allocatable pods
kubectl get node -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.allocatable.pods}{"\n"}{end}'

# Check EC2 quotas via AWS CLI
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A --region eu-west-1

# Describe instance network attributes
aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types p4d.24xlarge --region eu-west-1 --query 'InstanceTypes[0].NetworkInfo'
```

maria: Example quick sanity check output from a node: 

```
node-abc123 110
node-p4d-01 240
```

Note: those numbers are illustrative; p4d can support higher pods if trunking enabled.

alex: There's also CNI MTU issues with our inference traffic (large frames). Anyone hit fragmentation because of overlay CNI?

dana: Yes — if you use an overlay (Calico/IPIP or Flannel) default MTU often causes fragmentation for large protobuf payloads. We set MTU=8900 for jumbo frames on ENIs where supported, but that requires VPC + subnet support. If you rely on AWS NLB with TLS passthrough it's less of an issue.

ops-bot: AWS support case submitted: case-0123456789. Requested quotas: P4d +8, G5 +10, ENI +200, Secondary IPs +2048. ETA: 72 hours for initial review.

alex: awesome, thanks ops-bot. If they push back on ENI increases, what's Plan B?

maria: Plan B: use less-bursty IP usage — run multiple pods per IP via `hostNetwork` or `shared IP proxy` (but that complicates service discovery). Or use NAT gateway with node NATing (again tradeoffs). Another option: split workload across regions (eu-west-1 + eu-central-1) to avoid a single-region quota limit.

chen: Also consider using device plugin + pod annotation to pin GPU fraction (MIG) so you can safely pack more workloads on a physical GPU. That reduces node count and thus number of nodes * ENI overhead.

alex: Cost question: should we buy reserved instances for p4d now or start with spot and convert later?

dana: For steady-state 16 GPUs in prod we should do a reserved capacity contract (Dedicated or Savings Plan) — but start with spot/on-demand during testing. Reserved gives big discounts but requires commitment. We'll model cost after we get quota approval and a test run.

maria: I'll monitor the AWS case and if they ask for justification I'll supply our steady-state diagrams + expected throughput. Tagging @chen to follow up on nodegroup config with `eniConfig` and trunking enabled.

chen: I'll spin up a small test cluster with 1 p4d nodegroup and verify max pods, ENI trunking, and MTU behavior. ETA EOD.

alex: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll paste the final support case text into the ticket and attach our capacity plan. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Case updated: case-0123456789 -> AWS requested additional details about expected sustained network throughput. Please attach peak RPS and avg packet size in the support console.
